steps.why: Listing the branches is what separates omega from alpha, so the list carries the first mark.
common_mistakes: Writing only "all characters" without naming any branch.
Leaving out phylogenetic data, which the definition includes.
steps.memory_tip: Four of the extra branches end in -logy — embryology, cytology, palynology, serology — and the fifth is phytochemistry.
steps.margin_note: Name at least three branches. Two lines is enough here.

steps.why: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and this is the last, most complete stage of classifying a group.
common_mistakes: Calling omega taxonomy a separate branch of biology. It is a stage of taxonomy.
Saying it uses only molecular data.
steps.memory_tip: Alpha is the first Greek letter and the first look, the outside only. Omega is the last letter and uses everything.
steps.margin_note: One boxed sentence earns this mark. Do not write a paragraph.

insider_note: Alpha and omega taxonomy are asked as a pair. If you can state the contrast in one line you have both cards.
